newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed higher on Friday, but nowhere near as high as an early crown-driven rise in the early session woudl have indicated.
The declaration that Italy will apply to re-enter the exchange rate mechanism ERM in November entirely altered the scenario, dealers said.
"On top of that there was some interest in buying the crown at these levels", one dealer said.
"But even if we see some commercial flows next week, I don't think the crown firm to more than 4.38 against the D-mark due to the political risk," he added.
Six-month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 4.41 percent and the 10-year bond yields climbed two basis points to 7.24 percent, but both were higher in the morning.
Morning losses were driven foremost by the weaker crown, that had suffered along with other currences through uncertainity surrounding the French franc.
An S-E-Banken market letter in which the bank's chief economist warned that the government is losing its grip on the economy also added to the gloomy mood, dealers said.
An Italian linking of the lira to ERM will probably not have any major impact on the crown, economists and dealers told Reuters.
"I think people know that Sweden do not want to join ERM. Therefore, I don't think there will be any major effect on the crown," said Ian Ganna, economist at Chase.
The crown firmed to 4.4045 against the D-mark compared to 4.4125 late on Thursday.
